definitions.explanation: A reproduction or copy of an original document, text, or artwork. Used in administrative, legal, and everyday contexts for duplicated materials.

examples.japanese: {書類|しょるい}の{写|うつ}しを{取|と}る。
examples.english: To make a copy of a document.

examples.japanese: {戸籍|こせき}の{写|うつ}しを{役所|やくしょ}で{取得|しゅとく}した。
examples.english: I obtained a copy of the family register at the municipal office.

examples.japanese: この{手紙|てがみ}の{写|うつ}しは{何通|なんつう}か{残|のこ}っており、{研究者|けんきゅうしゃ}によって{分析|ぶんせき}されている。
examples.english: Several copies of this letter survive and are being analyzed by researchers.

notes:
The noun form of the verb {写|うつ}す (to copy). Refers to a copy or reproduction of a document, text, or other original. Common in administrative and historical contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {写|うつ}しを{取|と}る: to make a copy
- {戸籍|こせき}の{写|うつ}し: copy of a family register
- {原本|げんぽん}と{写|うつ}し: original and copy
- {写|うつ}しを{保管|ほかん}する: to keep a copy

SIMILAR WORDS:
- コピー: copy — the modern loanword, more casual and widely used in everyday contexts
- {複写|ふくしゃ}: reproduction, photocopy — a more formal term, often for mechanical reproduction
- {副本|ふくほん}: duplicate, carbon copy — used in legal and official contexts for official copies of documents
- {原本|げんぽん}: original — the opposite of a copy; the source document
